Capital One.

This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone.
President Trump is wrapping up the last weekend
before midterm elections with two rallies, one in Iowa,
one in Kansas.
In Michigan, the race for the Senate has taken a new twist
as a former Democratic primary hopeful
now says she is endorsing the Republican candidate.
NPR's Ava Berger reports.
Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens
broke with her party Sunday.
She posted on her social media that she
was endorsing Michigan's Republican candidate Mike
Rogers over fellow Democrat Abdul El Sayed.
I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today.
I don't belong in Abdul's campaign.
Stevens also endorsed Rogers outside of a church event
and said she still is a Democrat but didn't feel welcome
in El Sayed's campaign.
This split comes after El Sayed told reporters
he didn't want Stevens to attend a different church service
Sunday with him.
That was meant to show unity among Democrats.
In August, El Sayed beat Stevens in a bitter primary
in which the pair clashed over US support for Israel.
Initially, Stevens had endorsed El Sayed in the race.
Ava Berger, NPR News, Washington.
Democratic Senator Chris Murphy of Connecticut
is recovering after he was hospitalized this weekend
following a stroke, his office says.
Molly Ingram from member station WSHU reports.
A statement from his office says Murphy, who is 53 years old,
was at his son's hockey game Saturday
when he began to have numbness in his arm.
He was taken to a local hospital
where doctors discovered he had had a stroke.
The statement says he was then transferred
to Johns Hopkins for monitoring.
The statement goes on to say that Murphy is awake and alert
and responding well to treatment.
The three-term senator is not up for reelection this year
but has recently been traveling the country
campaigning for Democrats.
For NPR News, I'm Molly Ingram in Connecticut.
Iran's leaders say they will respond forcefully
to any attack on their country
even as the Iranian foreign minister pushes for diplomacy
and PR's Hidal al-Shalshi has more.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesman,
Hossein Muhabbi, told Iranian state media on Sunday
that there will be, quote, "no geographical limitations,"
end quote, during a possible war with the U.S. and Israel.
He said the directive came from Ayatollah Mushtaba Khamenei
who on Saturday said any threat to Iran
would face a, quote, "immediate and impactful response."
Muhabbi said the Revolutionary Guard has identified
new targets for a potential war
but did not provide details on what they were.
Meanwhile, during an interview with news network Al Jazeera,
Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araki, said Iran reached
a new proposal with mediators to reopen
the Strait of Hormuz in two days.
He did not elaborate on the details.
Hidal al-Shalshi, NPR News, Istanbul.
The United States and Israel have signaled
a potential return to hostilities
after the U.S. midterm elections Tuesday.
This is NPR News.
A Learjet carrying nine people crashed into a neighborhood
in South Florida early this afternoon.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says
all nine people have died.
A federal investigation of the crash is underway.
The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom Airport in Texas
and was headed for the Bahamas, according to the FAA.
Flash flooding has prompted mandatory evacuation orders
in parts of the Southwest.
Heavy rainfall in northern Arizona
has triggered flood warnings, highway closures,
and evacuations.
As member station KNAU's Ryan Heiches reports,
more than three inches of rain
have fallen since this morning.
First responders worked to rescue numerous people
stuck in their homes as waters rapidly rose in Oak Creek.
City of Sedona officials ordered residents and businesses
to evacuate as the waterways surged to near record levels.
It's impacted dozens of neighborhoods
and areas usually packed with tourists.
The National Weather Service has issued a flood warning
for much of northern and central Arizona.
In the last week, intense rain has hit most of the region,
including southwestern Colorado and the Navajo Nation.
Officials and advocates also worry that flooding,
washed out roads, and mud could complicate voting
for Tuesday's election in some rural and tribal areas.
For NPR News, I'm Ryan Heiches in Flagstaff.
In France, there's relief that weekend protests
over rising living costs resulted in less violence
than protests of recent weeks there.
Protests also erupted in other parts of Europe
led by young demonstrators.
I'm Louise Givoni, NPR News, Washington.

topics.text: Trump wraps midterm campaign weekend with rallies in Iowa and Kansas
Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate race over El Sayed
Senator Chris Murphy hospitalized after stroke, recovering at Johns Hopkins, office says
Iran's Revolutionary Guard vows no geographical limits in response to any attack
Iran's foreign minister says new proposal could reopen Strait of Hormuz in two days
US and Israel signal possible return to hostilities after Tuesday's midterm elections
Learjet crashes into South Florida neighborhood, killing all nine aboard, Duffy says
Flash flooding prompts evacuation orders in northern Arizona, including Sedona
